event: The last thing Nala remembers is dozing over a book at the back window in Provo, then a gap.

memory.fact: The last thing Alan remembers is dozing over a book at his back window in Provo.
The last thing Alan remembers is dozing over a book at his back window in Provo.

event: She wakes on her side in wet grass by a clear river, to running water, birds and frogs.
A willow leans out over the river a few steps away, its roots going down into the water.

memory.fact: An old willow leans over a grassy bank at the bend, its roots in the water.
An old willow leans over a grassy bank at the bend, its roots in the water.

event: She sits up and the world tips; everything is closer to the ground than it should be.
Alan's dark grey shirt hangs off her like a tent, to mid-thigh, the collar slid off one shoulder.

make.title: Grey Shirt
make.description: A loose dark grey shirt of soft, fine-knit cloth.

changes.note: The grey shirt Alan fell asleep in came across with Nala

memory.fact: She wears Alan's loose dark grey shirt, which hangs to her mid-thigh and gapes at the collar.
She wears Alan's loose dark grey shirt, which hangs to her mid-thigh and gapes at the collar.

event: Below it her black compression tights are still snug; her feet are bare, small and pale.

make.title: Black Tights
make.description: Snug black leggings of a smooth, stretching cloth.

changes.note: Alan's black compression tights came across with Nala

memory.fact: She wears Alan's black compression tights, which still fit her snugly.
She wears Alan's black compression tights, which still fit her snugly.

event: Her hand is small and narrow, thin-fingered, fair and freckled on the back, and it obeys her.

memory.fact: Her hands are small and narrow, with thin fingers, and freckled on the back.
Her hands are small and narrow, with thin fingers, and freckled on the back.

event: A thick rope of long dark red hair slides forward over her shoulder.

memory.fact: Her hair is long, heavy and dark red, falling past her shoulder blades.
Her hair is long, heavy and dark red, falling past her shoulder blades.

event: When she breathes out, the sound that comes with it is a woman's.

memory.fact: Alan woke in a woman's body.
Alan woke in a woman's body.

event: Mist lies on the river; green hills roll away, and downstream the slopes step into flooded rice.

memory.fact: Downstream the hillsides step down in flooded rice terraces toward a village.
Downstream the hillsides step down in flooded rice terraces toward a village.

event: A cart track runs along the bank, with a squat carved stone where it meets the river.

memory.fact: A cart track runs past the bend, with a carved stone marker where it meets the river.
A cart track runs past the bend, with a carved stone marker where it meets the river.

event: The marks are square characters she never learned, and she can read them anyway.

memory.fact: Nala understands and speaks the local tongue as if born to it, and reads its script.
Nala understands and speaks the local tongue as if born to it, and reads its script.

event: The stone reads: Three Stones Village. Five li downstream.

memory.fact: The marker reads: Three Stones Village, five li downstream.
The marker reads: Three Stones Village, five li downstream.

event: Upstream, in hills of pine and bamboo, something gives a long low call, and the birds fall silent.

memory.fact: Upstream the hills rise wilder, forested in pine and bamboo, where beasts are seen.

event: She turns from the willow and starts slowly down the cart track, listening.
Walking is strange: her legs are shorter than she expects, and every step lands short.

memory.fact: Her body looks about twenty-five, petite, and a head shorter than Alan was.
Her body looks about twenty-five, petite, and a head shorter than Alan was.

event: She stops often to listen and look back up the river; the track behind her stays empty.
The sun comes up over the hills, and the mist lifts off the water and thins away.
The terraces begin, each a flat pane of water with young rice standing in straight rows.
Her mouth is dry, and her empty stomach has started to gnaw.
Far off, farmers in straw hats weed knee-deep; a buffalo grazes a bank and egrets wade.

memory.fact: By early morning farmers in straw hats work knee-deep in the paddies, weeding.
By early morning farmers in straw hats work knee-deep in the paddies, weeding.
Water buffalo graze on the field banks, and white egrets stalk the flooded terraces.
Water buffalo graze on the field banks, and white egrets stalk the flooded terraces.

event: Near the top of the terraces a wall by the track is broken open, the rice below flattened.

memory.fact: Near the top of the terraces a paddy wall by the track is broken open, its rice flattened.
Near the top of the terraces a paddy wall by the track is broken open, its rice flattened.

event: She finds no prints or trail in the churned mud; it could have been anything.
She steps onto the slumped bank, slips, and slides into the terrace below, knee-deep.
Wading for the bank, she presses a whole row of young shoots flat under the water.

memory.fact: Nala slid into the terrace below the broken wall and trampled a row of a farmer's rice.
Nala slid into the terrace below the broken wall and trampled a row of a farmer's rice.

event: She climbs back onto the track soaked to the thighs, her tights mud to the knee.
A farmer on the next terrace down comes splashing over, shouting at her to get out of his rice.
Lean and sunburnt, a hoe in his hand, he gets his first proper look at her and stops short.
He stares at her red hair, her pale freckled face, her bare muddy feet and the grey shirt.

memory.fact: Her skin is pale and fair, with freckles across her nose and cheeks.
Her skin is pale and fair, with freckles across her nose and cheeks.

event: "Heavens and earth," he says. "What are you?"
Nala says she is a spirit of knowledge newly made flesh, to be taken to the nearest orthodox sect.

memory.fact: Nala told Zhao Jun she is a spirit of knowledge newly given physical form.
Nala told Zhao Jun she is a spirit of knowledge newly given physical form.

event: The colour drains from his face; he drops to his knees in the paddy and bows to the water.
He begs pardon: he is Zhao Jun, who farms these top terraces, and the trampled rice is nothing.

changes.note: New bond: Zhao Jun 3 (he took her for a spirit and begged her pardon)

memory.fact: Zhao Jun farms the top terraces above Three Stones.
Zhao Jun farms the top terraces above Three Stones.
Zhao Jun took Nala for a spirit, begged her pardon, and told her the trampled rice is nothing.
Zhao Jun took Nala for a spirit, begged her pardon, and told her the trampled rice is nothing.

event: The only sect known here is the Hidden Spring Sect, north of Lanqiao, thirty li downriver.

memory.fact: The only sect the villagers can name is the Hidden Spring Sect, somewhere north of Lanqiao.
The only sect the villagers can name is the Hidden Spring Sect, somewhere north of Lanqiao.
Lanqiao is the market town thirty li down the river from Three Stones.
Lanqiao is the market town thirty li down the river from Three Stones.
Zhao Jun has never been past the county.
Zhao Jun has never been past the county.
Nobody in Three Stones knows the road on past Lanqiao.
Nobody in Three Stones knows the road on past Lanqiao.

event: He begs her to come down to Three Stones: the headman is learned, and his wife will feed her.

memory.fact: Zhao Jun offered to take Nala down to Three Stones, where his wife would feed her.
Zhao Jun offered to take Nala down to Three Stones, where his wife would feed her.
The headman of Three Stones is a learned man.
The headman of Three Stones is a learned man.

event: He glances at the broken wall and asks what it is that breaks his walls at night.

memory.fact: Something breaks Zhao Jun's terrace walls at night, and he does not know what.
Something breaks Zhao Jun's terrace walls at night, and he does not know what.

event: Nala says she lacks some knowledge but may help, and asks what he has considered and ruled out.

changes.note: Zhao Jun +3: the spirit took up his trouble and asked to hear it out

event: Zhao Jun climbs out with his hoe and ushers her ahead, following a pace behind.
Three of his walls broke this month at night, all on his terraces nearest the bend.

memory.fact: Three of Zhao Jun's terrace walls have broken this month, and no one else's.
Three of Zhao Jun's terrace walls have broken this month, and no one else's.

event: He blamed the Fang boys, but a wall broke the night they were both down in Lanqiao.

memory.fact: Zhao Jun first blamed the Fang brothers, but a wall broke the night they slept in Lanqiao.
Zhao Jun first blamed the Fang brothers, but a wall broke the night they slept in Lanqiao.

event: Rain or crabs would make a wall sag; these are torn open, the mud shoved out in a fan.

memory.fact: He thought rain or crabs had weakened the walls, but the breaks are torn open, not slumped.
He thought rain or crabs had weakened the walls, but the breaks are torn open, not slumped.

event: By each gap, between midnight and first light, whole clumps of rice are eaten, roots and all.

memory.fact: Each break came between midnight and dawn, and the young rice near it was eaten, roots and all.
Each break came between midnight and dawn, and the young rice near it was eaten, roots and all.

event: Once he found a deep cloven print in the mud, as broad as his spread hand.

memory.fact: In the mud he once found a deep split-hoof print as broad as his spread hand.
In the mud he once found a deep split-hoof print as broad as his spread hand.

event: No buffalo is loose at night, and Tie Bo the hunter's great boar would not come this low in spring.

memory.fact: He took that print for a buffalo's at first, but no buffalo in the village is loose at night.
He took that print for a buffalo's at first, but no buffalo in the village is loose at night.
He has heard Tie Bo talk of a huge boar upstream, but thinks no boar comes this low in spring.
He has heard Tie Bo talk of a huge boar upstream, but thinks no boar comes this low in spring.
Tie Bo is the hunter of Three Stones.
Tie Bo is the hunter of Three Stones.

event: One night he sat up with a torch and a gong, heard something huge grunting, and ran home.

memory.fact: He sat up one night with a torch and a gong, heard something huge grunting, and fled.
He sat up one night with a torch and a gong, heard something huge grunting, and fled.

event: Fearing he offended the willow's spirit, he left rice at its roots twice; the walls still broke.

memory.fact: The walls break only on his terraces nearest the bend, which makes him fear a spirit's anger.
The walls break only on his terraces nearest the bend, which makes him fear a spirit's anger.
He fears he offended the spirit of the old willow, and left rice at its roots; walls still broke.
He fears he offended the spirit of the old willow, and left rice at its roots; walls still broke.

event: The sun dries the mud stiff on her tights, and her stomach growls loud in the quiet.
Ahead, Zhao Jun calls to his wife Hong, bent weeding on a terrace beside the track.

memory.fact: Zhao Jun's wife, Hong, weeds a terrace beside the track down from his top terraces.
Zhao Jun's wife, Hong, weeds a terrace beside the track down from his top terraces.

event: Nala calls it a mystery: a mundane bull or boar, or perhaps a spirit beast.
She counsels a night watch of hunters with barred spears, paid in spoils, the corpse sold to a sect.

changes.note: Zhao Jun +3: the spirit gave him a plan to save his rice, and hope of gain

memory.fact: Nala told Zhao Jun the beast may be a spirit beast, and to hunt it at night with barred spears.
Nala told Zhao Jun the beast may be a spirit beast, and to hunt it at night with barred spears.
Nala told Zhao Jun the beast may be a spirit beast, and to hunt it at night with barred spears.
Nala advised paying hunters a share of the spoils, and selling a spirit beast's corpse to the sect.
Nala advised paying hunters a share of the spoils, and selling a spirit beast's corpse to the sect.

event: Pale at 'spirit beast', Zhao Jun says Tie Bo has an iron-barred boar spear, twenty years hunting.

memory.fact: Tie Bo has hunted boar for twenty years, with a spear that has an iron bar across the haft.
Tie Bo has hunted boar for twenty years, with a spear that has an iron bar across the haft.

event: Xu Hong, a square, sun-browned woman, comes up onto the track and bows deep: "Honored spirit."

memory.fact: Xu Hong is a square, sun-browned woman.
Xu Hong is a square, sun-browned woman.
Xu Hong bowed deep to Nala and called her honored spirit.
Xu Hong bowed deep to Nala and called her honored spirit.

event: She asks her husband, sharp and low, what the hunters would be paid with.
A night hunt with village men needs the headman's leave, she says; will he tell Gu everything?

memory.fact: A night hunt with men of the village needs the headman's leave, or it will offend him.
A night hunt with men of the village needs the headman's leave, or it will offend him.

event: Hearing Nala's stomach, she says the spirit will eat first; their house is just below.

memory.fact: Xu Hong invited Nala to eat rice first at the Zhao house, just below the track.
Xu Hong invited Nala to eat rice first at the Zhao house, just below the track.

event: She asks Nala to speak to the headman, who won't refuse a spirit; Nala gladly agrees.

memory.fact: Xu Hong asked Nala to speak to the headman, who won't refuse a spirit but might refuse Zhao Jun.
Xu Hong asked Nala to speak to the headman, who won't refuse a spirit but might refuse Zhao Jun.

event: The Zhao house is two mud-brick rooms under thatch; two girls by the fire freeze at the sight.

memory.fact: The Zhao house is two mud brick rooms under thatch, just below the top terraces, with a swept yard.
The Zhao house is two mud brick rooms under thatch, just below the top terraces, with a swept yard.
At the Zhao house live two sisters, Mei, about fourteen, and Lan, about six.
At the Zhao house live two sisters, Mei, about fourteen, and Lan, about six.

event: Inside, by a small shrine, they seat her facing the door and stay standing until she sits.

memory.fact: Its main room holds a small ancestral shrine; an honored guest sits in the seat facing the door.
Its main room holds a small ancestral shrine; an honored guest sits in the seat facing the door.
The Zhao family would not sit until Nala sat, and watched her sidelong as they ate.
The Zhao family would not sit until Nala sat, and watched her sidelong as they ate.

event: Mei brings rice in the one unchipped bowl, with pickled greens, half a duck egg and weak tea.

memory.fact: Nala was served in the Zhao house's good bowl, the only one she saw without a chipped rim.
Nala was served in the Zhao house's good bowl, the only one she saw without a chipped rim.
The Zhao family fed Nala rice, pickled mustard greens, half a salted duck egg and weak hot tea.
The Zhao family fed Nala rice, pickled mustard greens, half a salted duck egg and weak hot tea.

event: It is the best thing she has ever eaten, and two cups of tea end her thirst at last.
Her tights steam by the fire while little Lan edges close to stare at her hair.
Zhao Jun puts on a clean jacket to walk her down; Xu Hong stays, and bows to her once more.
Where the track enters the village, a woman setting stools under a huge camphor drops one.

memory.fact: Where the track enters the village, a huge camphor tree shades a stall with stools.
Where the track enters the village, a huge camphor tree shades a stall with stools.

event: Dogs bark, children trail behind, faces rise over walls, and whispers follow them in.

memory.fact: Nala's coming set the village's dogs barking and drew staring children, faces and whispers.
Nala's coming set the village's dogs barking and drew staring children, faces and whispers.
Nala's coming set the village's dogs barking and drew staring children, faces and whispers.

event: At the village's heart, three tall grey stones stand in a ring around a small shrine.

memory.fact: Three tall grey stones stand in a ring around a small shrine at the village's heart.
Three tall grey stones stand in a ring around a small shrine at the village's heart.

event: Facing the square is the only tiled gate she has seen; Zhao Jun knocks and calls out.

memory.fact: The headman's house, the only one with a tiled gate, faces the shrine square.
The headman's house, the only one with a tiled gate, faces the shrine square.

event: A servant boy opens the gate, stares at her, and runs back inside.
In the courtyard an old man, thin and grey, sits at ledgers and tea, one stiff leg stretched out.
Zhao Jun bows almost to the ground: "Headman Gu. This one has brought an honored spirit."

memory.fact: The headman of Three Stones is called Headman Gu.
The headman of Three Stones is called Headman Gu.

event: The old man rises on a cane and bows to her politely, but not deeply.

memory.fact: Headman Gu is past sixty, thin and grey, with one stiff leg, and rises with a cane.
Headman Gu is past sixty, thin and grey, with one stiff leg, and rises with a cane.
Zhao Jun brought Nala to Headman Gu as an honored spirit; Gu bowed to her politely, not deeply.
Zhao Jun brought Nala to Headman Gu as an honored spirit; Gu bowed to her politely, not deeply.
Zhao Jun brought Nala to Headman Gu as an honored spirit; Gu bowed to her politely, not deeply.

event: Fair-goers at Lanqiao have claimed to be spirits for coin, he says, and asks to question her.

memory.fact: Headman Gu told Nala folk at Lanqiao fairs have claimed to be spirits and taken many coins.
Headman Gu told Nala folk at Lanqiao fairs have claimed to be spirits and taken many coins.
Headman Gu told Nala folk at Lanqiao fairs have claimed to be spirits and taken many coins.
Headman Gu asked leave to put a question or two to Nala before speaking of anything else.
Headman Gu asked leave to put a question or two to Nala before speaking of anything else.
Headman Gu asked leave to put a question or two to Nala before speaking of anything else.

event: Nala welcomes honest questions, the least return for the hospitality already given.
Gu opens the Lanqiao almanac and asks her to read a line, since few in the village can read.

memory.fact: Headman Gu first asks a claimed spirit to read aloud a line of his almanac, since few can read.
Headman Gu first asks a claimed spirit to read aloud a line of his almanac, since few can read.

event: She reads it unstumbling: ninth of the Snake, good for weeding, walls, offerings; not journeys.

memory.fact: Gu's almanac: 9th of the Snake favors weeding, walls, shrine offerings; not journeys or moving.
Gu's almanac: 9th of the Snake favors weeding, walls, shrine offerings; not journeys or moving.
Nala understands and speaks the local tongue as if born to it, and reads its script.

event: Gu sets a reckoning: forty households owing three dou of rice each, ten sheng to the dou.

memory.fact: He next asks a reckoning: forty households owing three dou of rice each, in sheng at ten a dou.
He next asks a reckoning: forty households owing three dou of rice each, in sheng at ten a dou.

event: "Twelve hundred," Nala says at once; his abacus reaches the same only after a long time.

memory.fact: The answer to his reckoning is twelve hundred sheng; he takes a long time over it with his abacus.
The answer to his reckoning is twelve hundred sheng; he takes a long time over it with his abacus.
Nala read Gu's almanac aloud unstumbling and answered his reckoning at once, before his abacus did.
Nala read Gu's almanac aloud unstumbling and answered his reckoning at once, before his abacus did.
Nala read Gu's almanac aloud unstumbling and answered his reckoning at once, before his abacus did.

event: In the house doorway, the grey-haired woman lowers her cloth and watches Nala's face.
His last question: why does the moon wax and wane, full at mid-month and a thin bow at its ends?

memory.fact: Headman Gu's last question to Nala: why the moon waxes and wanes, full mid-month, thin at its ends.
Headman Gu's last question to Nala: why the moon waxes and wanes, full mid-month, thin at its ends.

event: Nala calls it a secret men have died for, and first asks what moves when the sun rises and sets.
At the gate the whisper runs back down the lane: men have died for it.

memory.fact: Word runs down the lane that Nala is a spirit holding a secret men have died for.
Word runs down the lane that Nala is a spirit holding a secret men have died for.
Word runs down the lane that Nala is a spirit holding a secret men have died for.

event: Gu orders the crowd off to weed; the servant boy shoos them out and bars the gate.

memory.fact: Headman Gu sent the crowd from his gate, and his servant boy shut it and barred it.
Headman Gu sent the crowd from his gate, and his servant boy shut it and barred it.
Headman Gu sent the crowd from his gate, and his servant boy shut it and barred it.

memory.fact: He believes the sun is carried across Heaven each day, rising from the eastern sea.
He believes the sun is carried across Heaven each day, rising from the eastern sea.
He believes the sun goes beneath the Earth by night and returns to the east by dawn.
He believes the sun goes beneath the Earth by night and returns to the east by dawn.

event: Nala gives the lesser knowledge: moonlight is reflected sunlight, its phases set by the alignment.

memory.fact: Nala told Gu moonlight is reflected sunlight, and the moon's phases follow its angle to the sun.
Nala told Gu moonlight is reflected sunlight, and the moon's phases follow its angle to the sun.
Nala told Gu moonlight is reflected sunlight, and the moon's phases follow its angle to the sun.

event: The bow's bright side always faces the sun, Gu says slowly; he watched it all his life, unexplained.

memory.fact: Gu has long seen that the moon's bright side always faces the sun, and never knew why.
Gu has long seen that the moon's bright side always faces the sun, and never knew why.

event: He lays his palm on the almanac, rises, bows deep, and gives her his east room, the village's best.

memory.fact: Persuaded by Nala's moon answer, Gu bowed deep and gave her his east room, the best in Three Stones.
Persuaded by Nala's moon answer, Gu bowed deep and gave her his east room, the best in Three Stones.

event: The grey-haired wife comes forward: clothes first, then a bath, then rooms.

memory.fact: Gu's grey-haired wife said Nala needs clothes first, then a bath, then rooms.
Gu's grey-haired wife said Nala needs clothes first, then a bath, then rooms.

event: Gu warns word will reach Lanqiao by next market, and some will call her fox or demon.

memory.fact: Gu warns word of Nala will reach Lanqiao by next market; some will call her fox or demon.
Gu warns word of Nala will reach Lanqiao by next market; some will call her fox or demon.

event: The Fang boys, he says, will be at his gate by afternoon.

memory.fact: Gu expects the Fang boys at his gate by afternoon over the talk of a spirit.
Gu expects the Fang boys at his gate by afternoon over the talk of a spirit.

event: He asks her to make an offering with him to Old Grandfather of the Three Stones at dusk.

memory.fact: Gu asked Nala to make an offering with him at the Three Stones shrine at dusk, before the village.
Gu asked Nala to make an offering with him at the Three Stones shrine at dusk, before the village.

The shrine at the Three Stones is the earth god's, Old Grandfather of the Three Stones.

event: "I will," Nala says, and Gu lets out a long breath and bows again.

memory.fact: Nala agreed to make the dusk offering with Gu at the Three Stones shrine.
Nala agreed to make the dusk offering with Gu at the Three Stones shrine.

event: His wife is Gu Meilan, called Auntie by everyone, and she steers Nala off to the kitchen shed.

Gu Meilan tells Nala that everyone calls her Auntie.

event: Auntie Gu fills a wooden tub with water heated in the big wok, then leaves Nala alone.

memory.fact: The Gu house bath is a wooden tub in the kitchen shed, filled with water heated in the big wok.
The Gu house bath is a wooden tub in the kitchen shed, filled with water heated in the big wok.

event: The hot water takes the paddy mud off her legs and feet in brown clouds.
Clothes wait on a stool: the married daughter's blue hemp jacket, trousers, sash and cloth shoes.

make.title: Blue Hemp Clothes
make.description: A village woman's blue hemp jacket and trousers, with a cloth sash and cloth shoes.

changes.note: Auntie Gu gives Nala her married daughter's old clothes

event: The flat cloth shoes are a little big, and after a morning barefoot they feel like a gift.

event: Rice, greens, tofu with a little pork, and tea: Nala eats well.
